background: ABN AMRO is a Dutch retail, private and commercial bank, part-owned by the Dutch state since its rescue, funded largely by domestic deposits and lending mainly on Dutch residential mortgages and to Northwest European businesses.
synthesis: Ratings are A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, with one of the three on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook after a two-notch upgrade by one of them on 12 May 2026. Capital is the weaker side of the profile, CET1 of 15.3% and leverage of 4.9% both below their peer medians, while liquidity is strong, with LCR of 159% above the median and NSFR of 138% in the top quarter. Since 30 Jun 2025 CET1 has risen 0.8 points and LCR 14 points, but leverage has fallen 0.6 points and NSFR is broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged items, both on 12 Aug 2026, are a profit beat and raised guidance, set against an older item on anti-money-laundering shortcomings.
